generationContext.text:
# Azure AI Discovery client library for .NET

Azure AI Discovery lets you build investigation and knowledge-base experiences on top of your
Discovery workspace. The client library exposes two top-level clients:

- `WorkspaceClient` — conversations, investigations, tasks, and tools.
- `BookshelfClient` — knowledge bases (create, list, index, search, delete).

## Getting started

### Install the package

Install the client library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.AI.Discovery --prerelease
```

### Prerequisites

- You must have a [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).
- An existing Azure AI Discovery workspace and bookshelf endpoint.

### Authenticate the client

The library uses [`Azure.Identity`](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/overview/azure/identity-readme)
for authentication. `DefaultAzureCredential` works for most scenarios, including local development.

```C# Snippet:Discovery_CreateClients
Uri workspaceEndpoint = new Uri("<workspace-endpoint>");
WorkspaceClient workspaceClient = new WorkspaceClient(workspaceEndpoint, new DefaultAzureCredential());

Uri bookshelfEndpoint = new Uri("<bookshelf-endpoint>");
BookshelfClient bookshelfClient = new BookshelfClient(bookshelfEndpoint, new DefaultAzureCredential());
```

## Key concepts

- **`WorkspaceClient`** is the entry point for workspace operations. Use its `Get*Client()` methods to
  obtain the sub-clients: `GetDiscoveryConversationsClient()`, `GetDiscoveryInvestigationsClient()`,
  `GetDiscoveryTasksClient()`, and `GetDiscoveryToolsClient()`.
- **`BookshelfClient`** is the entry point for knowledge-base operations via
  `GetKnowledgeBasesClient()`.
- **Long-running operations** (for example `KnowledgeBases.CreateOrUpdate` and `KnowledgeBases.Delete`)
  return an `Operation`; pass `WaitUntil.Completed` to wait for the operation to finish, or
  `WaitUntil.Started` to poll manually.

## Examples

See the [samples](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/discovery/Azure.AI.Discovery/samples/README.md) for end-to-end usage. A minimal example that creates and reads a
conversation:

```C# Snippet:Discovery_CreateAndReadConversation
DiscoveryConversationsClient conversationsClient = workspaceClient.GetDiscoveryConversationsClient();

DiscoveryConversation created = await conversationsClient.CreateAsync(
    projectName: "my-project",
    investigationName: "/projects/my-project/investigations/my-investigation",
    displayName: "Getting started conversation");

DiscoveryConversation conversation = await conversationsClient.GetAsync(created.Name);
Console.WriteLine($"Conversation: {conversation.Name}");
```

## Troubleshooting

Service operations throw a `RequestFailedException` on failure, with a `Status` code and an
error `Message` that can be used to diagnose the failure.

## Next steps

Browse the [samples](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/discovery/Azure.AI.Discovery/samples/README.md) for more scenarios covering investigations, tasks, tools, and
knowledge bases.

## Contributing

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately (for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct](https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/). For more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ](https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/faq/) or contact [opencode@microsoft.com](mailto:opencode@microsoft.com) with any other questions or comments.

proposals.subtype: Replace synchronous create/update with the resource-provisioning operation
proposals.explanation: The suppressed generated CreateOrUpdate signature is replaced by a method validating name/content, sending the create/update request and constructing ProvisioningStateOperation with the response, resource name and context. WaitUntil.Completed invokes WaitForCompletion with the context cancellation token. The method records diagnostic failures and rethrows.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Customization-path source contains CodeGenSuppress for the exact method and a concrete replacement body.

proposals.subtype: Replace asynchronous create/update with a provisioning-state operation
proposals.explanation: CreateOrUpdateAsync validates name/content, awaits ProcessMessageAsync, wraps the initial response in ProvisioningStateOperation and optionally awaits WaitForCompletionAsync when Completed is requested. It passes the resource name/context to the custom operation and marks diagnostic failures before rethrowing.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The supplied customization file suppresses the generated async signature and implements its replacement.

proposals.subtype: Replace synchronous delete with a delete-until-gone operation
proposals.explanation: Delete validates knowledgeBaseName, sends CreateDeleteRequest and constructs DeleteUntilGoneOperation with the response and resource identity/context. It calls WaitForCompletionResponse only for WaitUntil.Completed, with the context token, and records/rethrows diagnostic failures.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: CodeGenSuppress explicitly removes the generated delete signature and the customization file provides the replacement.

proposals.subtype: Replace asynchronous delete with delete-until-resource-404 polling
proposals.explanation: DeleteAsync validates the resource name, awaits the delete request, constructs DeleteUntilGoneOperation and optionally awaits WaitForCompletionResponseAsync for Completed. It forwards context/cancellation and rethrows after marking diagnostic failure.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: An explicit generated-signature suppression and full async body occur in the marked customization file.

proposals.subtype: Implement a resource-GET delete operation that completes only on HTTP 404
proposals.explanation: DeleteUntilGoneOperation retains client/name/context/initial response and exposes the resource name as Id. Sync/async status updates return the retained response after completion; otherwise they GET the named resource through GetForPolling and set completion only when status is 404. The GET helpers call Pipeline.Send/SendAsync and return message.Response rather than ProcessMessage. The local operation has no explicit branch marking other status codes failed.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete Customization-path Operation subclass and its concrete raw-GET helpers are supplied as handwritten-marker evidence.

proposals.subtype: Implement resource-provisioning completion with explicit state precedence and synchronous shortcut
proposals.explanation: ProvisioningStateOperation treats absence of Operation-Location as completed and stores initial content without a local HTTP-status check. With the header it evaluates initial state without throwing on failure. Subsequent sync/async updates GET the named resource, prefer a string provisioningState over string status and recognize Succeeded/Failed/Canceled case-insensitively. Success stores content; failure marks completed and throws only when evaluation requested throwing. Missing/unparseable state leaves state unchanged. Value throws when no value is available. The helper returns null for empty, non-object or malformed JSON. Operation-Location is tested for presence, not used as the polling URL.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The supplied marked customization class implements Operation<BinaryData>, including constructor, status updates, value semantics and state evaluation; the parser/GET helper bodies are also supplied.

decisions.reason: The cited suppression and replacement CreateOrUpdate body construct the handwritten provisioning-state operation and wait conditionally. This is a concrete LRO override, not merely a generated poller; the reusable custom-poller pattern and potential generator support are appropriate.

The exact async signature is suppressed and the cited handwritten method awaits the request, constructs ProvisioningStateOperation and conditionally waits. Its symbol and lines identify the async implementation separately from the synchronous method.

The cited suppression and Delete implementation show a handwritten replacement that returns DeleteUntilGoneOperation and optionally waits for completion. The custom-poller category and pattern describe the source rather than relying on the comment's unverified account of service behavior.

The cited async Delete body is a suppressed, handwritten LRO wrapper that awaits the delete request and, for Completed, the resource-404 operation. The cited lines and symbol match the implementation.

The non-generated Operation subclass actually GETs the resource synchronously and asynchronously, marking completion on 404; the cited GetForPolling helpers send those GET requests. Its exact lines, category, and reusable custom-poller pattern are supported.

The handwritten Operation<BinaryData> evaluates provisioning state, handles a missing Operation-Location header, polls by resource GET and handles terminal states; the cited parser shows provisioningState precedence with status fallback. The proposal distinguishes actual code from the unsupported service-root-cause comment.

CodeGenType("ByType") on the otherwise empty, non-generated DiscoveryActorType declaration is an explicit handwritten generator type-name override, not empty scaffolding without behavior. The naming pattern can in principle be addressed by generator or TypeSpec naming rules.

The non-generated InfrastructureOverrides class explicitly maps CodeGenType("InfraOverrides"); although its body is empty, the attribute changes the intended generated type name. The finding does not claim a custom implementation or wire-format change.

The cited CodeGenType("NodepoolUsage") attribute on NodePoolUsage is an explicit naming override in a customization file. The proposal confines its claim to casing/name and does not infer generated members.

RunOperationStatus is a non-generated declaration with CodeGenType("OperationStatusRunResultError"); this is an explicit generated-name mapping, despite the empty body. The proposed subtype and pattern do not misclassify it as custom polling.

The handwritten static Nfs property and CodeGenMember("NFS") annotation are present at the cited lines. This is a member-name/API-shape override; the finding correctly avoids asserting an unseen definition of NFSValue or generated wire behavior.

The non-generated SupercomputerUsage partial class declares NodePools and maps it to "Nodepools" using CodeGenMember. The evidence supports the public member declaration and naming override, not a proven change from the unseen generated type.

limitations: Coverage is partial: nine of 172 eligible files from 190 discovered files are captured. All nine are supplied as handwritten-marker evidence under Customization, but this does not exhaust other library behavior.

The four operation entrypoint replacements are separate supplied methods; each custom Operation class is one coherent poller implementation. GetForPolling, GetForPollingAsync, ReadProvisioningState and accessors support the pollers and are not counted again as standalone transport, serialization or operation-ID customizations.

Comments claim the generated monitor is broken, default Azure.Core status selection would poll forever and analogous fixes ship in other languages. No server traces, original generated bodies or other SDK implementations substantiate those causal/comparative claims here.

The provisioning constructor's no-header shortcut does not itself require status 200 despite its comment. Initial Failed/Canceled evaluation marks completion without throwing, and later status updates return immediately when complete. These are literal local branches, not end-to-end failure/wait-method diagnoses.

ReadProvisioningState accepts a string provisioningState even if empty/unknown before considering status, and catches JsonException to return null. Nonterminal/missing states and unexpected delete response codes have no additional local completion/failure mapping in the supplied classes. No network behavior was exercised.

Request builders, Pipeline.Send/ProcessMessage behavior, Azure.Core Operation wait implementations and generated model serialization are absent. In particular, the source comment about Send returning non-success responses is not treated as proof of every pipeline's behavior.

CodeGenType declarations rename types rather than replace generated model implementations. CodeGenMember declarations show public mappings, not proof of changed wire values, deep immutability or generated baseline types.
Library latestRelease 1.0.0-beta.1 differs from csproj 1.0.0-beta.2. Shared-source includes and README Operation examples do not independently prove further custom LRO implementations.
No SDK code was executed or externally fetched. Generator addressability is plausible for explicit LRO state/completion semantics and naming hooks, not proof of current emitter support.
Only nine source files were captured from 172 eligible files; this assessment covers supplied evidence and cannot establish the absence of additional SDK customizations.

Generated counterpart files, TypeSpec definitions and runtime service behavior are not supplied. Type/member mappings and service-workaround motivations cannot be independently compared or confirmed; explanatory comments are not proof of a broken operation-status endpoint.

ReadProvisioningState and GetForPolling are implementation details of the proposed LRO behaviors, not independently counted omissions on the supplied evidence. Accepted decisions denote AI review, not human verification; human review may override them.
